reviews.pros: There is nothing to like about Hexaware.
reviews.cons:
I had a disappointing experience at Hexaware in just 3 months while working for Athena process. The company presents a completely different picture during hiring, but the reality is far from it.
Misleading Hiring Process: HRs promise one job role but assign you to another. They claim you’ll receive a net monthly salary based on Rating 3, but after joining, you’ll realize you’re getting Rating 2. They also rush employees into signing the VPA structure, which isn’t transparent.
Exploitative Work Schedule: Despite being promised two weekly offs, you’re forced to work on weekends under the excuse of "business requirements." Public holidays listed in the company calendar are also denied.
Unrealistic Training & No Support: The HR team states one month of training, but it’s cut down to 15 days to meet business demands. During OJT, there is minimal support, yet you’re expected to meet targets even after shift hours.
Toxic Operations Team & Management: The managers and operations team are unprofessional, arrogant, and unhelpful. They constantly push employees to work extra hours and cancel planned leaves.
Poor Employee Facilities & No Lockers: Hexaware at Navi Mumbai MBP follows a strict no-phone policy, but they don’t provide lockers for employees. Instead, you must submit your phone to security daily and collect a token. If you need your phone during breaks, you must stand in a queue, collect it, and submit it again before returning. This process often eats into your break time, leaving employees frustrated. FOR VOICE PROCESS:- "ONCE YOU SUBMIT YOUR PHONE AT THE START OF THE SHIFT, YOU WILL GET YOUR PHONE DIRECTLY AFTER THE SHIFT". YOU ARE NOT ALLOWED TO TAKE PHONE IN BREAKS.
High Attrition & Unethical Practices: They mass-hire between January to April for peak season and later neglect employees, leading to high attrition. You’re left with no choice but to resign.
Bottom Line: If you value work-life balance, transparency, and fair management, this is not the right place.

questions.question: What are the strategies to handle SQL deadlocks?
questions.answer: Strategies to handle SQL deadlocks include prevention, detection, and resolution techniques to ensure smooth database operations.1. Use proper indexing to reduce the chances of deadlocks by speeding up query execution.2. Implement a consistent locking order across transactions to avoid circular wait conditions.3. Set a timeout for transactions to automatically roll back if they are waiting too long for a lock.4. Use the SQL Server deadlock graph to analyze and understand deadlock scenarios for better prevention.5. Optimize queries to reduce the duration of locks held on resources.
